title: Functional analysis of plant disease progress curves
text: plant disease epidemiology, temporal disease progress data frequently condensed single scalar summaries final severity Area Disease Progress Curve (AUDPC). convenient, scalar reductions collapse temporal dimension, discarding critical information epidemic onset, peak progress rates, acceleration phases, trajectory shapes. r4pde functional analysis framework treats disease progress curves continuous functional data modeled via Generalized Additive Models (GAMs). modular API enables researchers fit smoothed trajectories, compute instantaneous rates progress, measure whole-curve distances, perform functional PCA, quantify resistance indices, evaluate environmental stability:

title: Functional analysis of plant disease progress curves
text: Scientific question: multi-environment trials (locations, years) available, genotypes exhibit stable epidemic suppression versus high genotype--environment variability? epidemics monitored across multiple locations seasons (using environment parameter functional_curves()), functional_instability() computes Normalized Functional Instability (NFI): \[nFI_g = \frac{\frac{1}{E_g} \sum_{e=1}^{E_g} \int_T (f_{ge}(t) - \bar{f}_g(t))^2 dt}{\int_T \bar{f}_g(t)^2 dt}\] can also decompose instability spatial (location-driven) temporal (year--year) components via env_sep.

text: overall instability metric defined mean integrated squared deviation genotype--environment curve genotype-specific mean curve across environments, normalized integrated squared mean curve. Let \(f_{ge}(t)\) denote predicted epidemic trajectory genotype \(g\) environment \(e\), let \(\bar f_g(t)\) denote mean trajectory genotype \(g\) across environments. Functional instability computed : $$ FI_g = \frac{1}{E_g}\sum_{e=1}^{E_g} \int_T \left(f_{ge}(t)-\bar f_g(t)\right)^2 dt $$ normalized : $$ nFI_g = \frac{FI_g}{\int_T \bar f_g(t)^2 dt} $$ Numerical integration performed trapezoidal rule regular prediction grid observed time domain. Model requirements. genotype--environment curves \(f_{ge}(t)\) predicted fitted GAM environment genotype--environment terms included. model genotype--environment term (default functional_curves(ge_term = "none") environment random intercept), every genotype receives environment shift link scale; nFI mostly reflects genotype's disease level (low-disease genotypes appear unstable) warning given. Experimental-unit random intercepts averaged , unless units genotype x environment curves , case kept G x E term.

title: Instantaneous Disease Progress Rates from Functional Curves — functional_rate
text: Mathematical Formulation: Let \(S(t)\) denote fitted disease trajectory \(\eta(t) = X(t)\beta\) linear predictor GAM model, \(\mu(t) = g^{-1}(\eta(t))\). derivative link scale estimated : $$D = \frac{X(t + \epsilon) - X(t - \epsilon)}{2\epsilon}$$ $$\eta'(t) = D \beta$$ variance \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta'(t)) = \operatorname{diag}(D V_p D^T)\), \(V_p\) Bayesian posterior covariance matrix GAM parameters. response scale (scale = "response"), derivative mean trajectory : $$S'(t) = \frac{\mu(\eta(t + \epsilon)) - \mu(\eta(t - \epsilon))}{2\epsilon}$$ approximate gradient vector \(G\) respect \(\beta\) : $$G = \frac{\mu'(\eta(t + \epsilon)) X(t + \epsilon) - \mu'(\eta(t - \epsilon)) X(t - \epsilon)}{2\epsilon}$$ \(\mu'(\eta) = d\mu/d\eta\) given family$mu.eta(). uncertainty : $$\operatorname{Var}(S'(t)) = \operatorname{diag}(G V_p G^T)$$ Boundary Handling: observed boundaries \(t_{min}\) \(t_{max}\), one-sided forward backward differences used prevent unintended extrapolation beyond observed domain. Time-Invariant Terms Random Effects: Intercepts, main treatment effects, terms constant respect time cancel analytically \(X(t + \epsilon) - X(t - \epsilon)\). Environmental experimental unit random effects excluded default yield population-adjusted treatment rates, consistent functional_curves. -Epidemic Flat Curves: Curves observed response values equal zero (estimated rates numerical tolerance \(10^{-6}\)) explicitly return \(r_{max} = 0\), \(t_{r_{max}} = \text{NA}\), \(\text{growth\_duration} = 0\), \(\text{cumulative\_positive\_growth} = 0\).

title: Plot the output of temporal compartmental epidemic models — plot_model_results
code: # A simple HLIR model integrated with Euler steps # (the book uses deSolve::ode()) hlir <- function(beta = 0.3, p = 5, i = 10, H0 = 99, I0 = 1,                  days = 100, dt = 0.1) {   n <- days / dt + 1   out <- data.frame(time = seq(0, days, by = dt), H = H0, L = 0, I = I0, R = 0)   for (k in 2:n) {     s <- out[k - 1, ]     inf <- beta * s$H * s$I / (s$H + s$L + s$I + s$R)     out$H[k] <- s$H - dt * inf     out$L[k] <- s$L + dt * (inf - s$L / p)     out$I[k] <- s$I + dt * (s$L / p - s$I / i)     out$R[k] <- s$R + dt * s$I / i   }   out } res <- hlir() plot_model_results(res, type = "HLIR")   # Return the plot without printing, then modify it p <- plot_model_results(res, type = "HLIR", print = FALSE) p + ggplot2::labs(title = "HLIR model, beta = 0.3")   # Multi-seasonal epidemic: three seasons with increasing inoculum multi <- list(   n.yr = 3,   results = lapply(1:3, function(k) hlir(I0 = k, days = 120, dt = 0.5)),   inoc = c(1, 2, 3),   n.max = 100 ) plot_model_results(multi, type = "MULTI")

title: Fit the one-stage hierarchical model for SAD validation — sad_fit

Random-effects structures: full (0 + method + method:z | rater) + (1 | image) + (1 | image:condition): random intercept slope per rater method, correlated, image effect (intrinsic difficulty) image x condition effect. noim full without image x condition effect. sep (0 + method | rater) + (0 + method:z | rater) + (1 | image): intercepts slopes uncorrelated. base (1 + z | rater) + (1 | image): rater effects common methods. dispersion formula ~ condition * (z + (z^2)) ~ condition * z.
